headline: Networks prepared Black leaders; employers made the appointments
summary: The record includes collective leadership development and specific corporate appointments. Mentorship, training, a board seat and the chief executive role are separate steps, with different decision-makers.
coverageNote: Four selected episodes involving the Executive Leadership Council, TIAA-CREF and Xerox. No sequence here establishes that an ELC program caused either executive appointment.
question: What appointment filing, succession record or leadership-program outcome connects this history to your company?

events.title: Black executives form a professional leadership network
events.people: Alvaro L. Martins, Elynor Williams and fellow ELC founders
events.decisionMaker: Nineteen corporate executives formed the Executive Leadership Council
events.barrier: ELC’s history describes the limited routes available to Black executives reaching senior corporate leadership.
events.change: Martins convened peers to support Bishop College; the group also formed a continuing network of Black executives.
events.outcome: The Executive Leadership Council became an organization for supporting and developing Black corporate leadership.
events.limit: A network’s existence does not establish appointment authority at member companies; the college they initially supported closed in 1988.

source.title: Executive Leadership Council · History
source.locator: Alvaro Martins, Bishop College and nineteen founders paragraphs

events.title: Clifton Wharton leads TIAA-CREF
events.decisionMaker: TIAA-CREF; the archival exhibit does not reproduce the appointment votes
events.barrier: The reviewed exhibit documents the role and tenure but does not establish the company’s selection criteria or earlier candidate exclusions.
events.change: After leading Michigan State and the State University of New York, Wharton became TIAA-CREF chairman and CEO.
events.outcome: Michigan State’s archival exhibit records his service in those positions from 1987 to 1993.
events.limit: This is a documented Black executive’s career, not proof of an organization-wide change in promotion or a direct path for another employee.

source.title: Michigan State University Archives · Clifton R. Wharton Jr.
source.locator: Closing biographical paragraph covering TIAA-CREF service

events.title: A program prepares Black professionals for executive responsibility
events.people: Black managers, directors, vice presidents and other participants in Strengthening the Pipeline
events.decisionMaker: Executive Leadership Council; ELC members and employer HR leaders recommended participants
events.barrier: The program addressed preparation for advancement through coaching, mentoring and access to experienced Black executives.
events.change: ELC created Strengthening the Pipeline, with leadership training, assessments and career planning.
events.outcome: A 2019 program profile reported 814 completions and promotions for 10% of participants within three months of finishing.
events.limit: These are reported program outcomes, not a controlled estimate of its effect; completion did not guarantee promotion and employers retained hiring authority.

source.title: Center for Talent Innovation / ELC · Being Black in Corporate America
source.locator: Strengthening the Pipeline profile, PDF page 55

events.title: Xerox’s board elects Ursula Burns chief executive
events.people: Ursula M. Burns and outgoing CEO Anne M. Mulcahy
events.barrier: The transition from company president to chief executive required a board decision; a professional network could not confer the role.
events.change: On May 21, the board elected Burns CEO with an effective date of July 1, 2009.
events.outcome: The company filed the decision publicly; Mulcahy was to remain board chair, distinguishing the two positions.
events.limit: The filing establishes an appointment decision at Xerox, not a change in hiring rules for every Black employee or an appointment at another employer.

sources.title: Smithsonian NMAAHC · Ursula Burns and her Xerox career
sources.locator: Opening paragraph and Historically Speaking program description, July 1, 2021

furtherResearch: Find appointment filings and board or succession records for the exact company and role; distinguish corporate officers, directors and line managers.
Check access to sponsorship, development programs and actual promotions using employer records, rather than inferring access from a prominent executive’s biography.
Research Black corporate leadership before these selected examples and document barriers and reversals alongside appointments.
